review_notes:
I read the whole file. The declarations are the Spec-of-coordinate-ring scheme and its finite-type and quasi-compact instances, the group object, `generalLinearGroupFunctor`, the points functor, the convolution/matrix comparison equivalences, and the natural isomorphism.

I searched Mathlib for competing concepts: a functor from algebras to groups sending R to GL_n(R), a GL group scheme, and other uses of `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map`. I found no such functor or scheme. Mathlib has `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup.map` only as a plain homomorphism, and `generalLinearGroupFunctor` wraps it into a `CommAlgCat K ⥤ GrpCat`. The file builds on existing Mathlib pieces instead of redefining them: `Spec.mapMulEquiv`, `WithConv`, `AlgHom.convMul_apply`, `yonedaGrp`, `algSpec`, and `Grp` in `Over`.

Elsewhere in this repository, `generalLinearModuleFunctor` is a separate formulation for modules, and the sibling group functors (diagonal, upper triangular and so on) are different groups. These are not Mathlib duplicates, and I could not show that consolidation would pay off. The one thing I did not investigate is whether the new functor could be derived from an existing Mathlib units-of-matrix-ring functor; I found none.
